metadata.title: Noemorph consciousness and mind research corpus
metadata.methodology: A citation-first, open-world collection organized from Robert Lawrence Kuhn's inclusive 2024 landscape, the 474-entry Closer To Truth Landscape index, systematic and scoping reviews, primary works, and authoritative scholarly references. Dated research supplements extend independently audited strata while retaining theory boundaries, source roles, evidence profiles, open questions, and collection provenance. Discovery-frame candidates remain separate from reviewed catalog records, and conceptual synthesis remains deferred.
metadata.coverage_notice: There is no defensible fixed denominator for ‘all theories.’ Noemorph reports protocol coverage, unresolved strata, and discovery yield rather than declaring the catalog complete.

discovery_frames.name: TSC 2024 research-topic taxonomy
discovery_frames.type: Scope-control taxonomy; topics are not counted as theories

gate_requirements: Every published catalog record has at least two retained citation locators and exact destinations.
Scientific theories, philosophical positions, frameworks, traditions, and social-cognition theories remain separately typed.
Citation title, author, work identity, and DOI destination pass independent semantic review.
At least 95% of registered discovery-frame items are screened overall and 85% in every mandatory stratum.
At least 90% of records are anchored to a primary or authoritative self-exposition source, or reviewed waiver.
Unresolved identity and duplicate candidates fall below the protocol threshold.
Two independent reviewers approve the coverage report before synthesis begins.

records.status_note: A proposed physical characterization, not evidence that such a state has been identified in brains.
records.summary: Consciousness is hypothesized as a state of matter distinguished by information, integration, independence, dynamics, and utility principles, generalizing IIT-like ideas to arbitrary physical systems.
records.scope: See cited definition and scope review

records.domain: Mathematical psychology / idealist or consciousness-first metaphysics
records.tradition: Mathematical psychology / idealist or consciousness-first metaphysics
records.status_note: Formal agent dynamics and consciousness-first interpretation should be stored as separate claim records.
records.summary: Reality is modeled as networks of interacting conscious agents; spacetime and physical objects are proposed to emerge from their dynamics rather than consciousness emerging from spacetime.

records.name: Interface Theory of Perception (ITP)
records.status_note: ITP is a theory of perception and does not entail Conscious Agent Theory without additional premises.
records.summary: Perception is evolutionarily shaped as a fitness-guiding user interface rather than a veridical depiction of objective structure.
records.scope: See cited definition and scope review

records.name: Consciousness-causes-collapse (London–Bauer / Wigner family)
records.status: historical · largely rejected in physics · speculative
records.status_note: Do not call this the “von Neumann–Wigner interpretation” without qualification; SEP notes that von Neumann’s position is often conflated with Wigner’s.
records.summary: Conscious awareness is assigned a special role in completing quantum measurement or collapse; Wigner later distanced himself from the view.
records.scope: See cited definition and scope review

records.name: Leibnizian monadology and pre-established harmony
records.status_note: Monad perceptions range from obscure to apperceptive; do not equate every monad with human consciousness.
records.summary: Reality consists of simple, perception-bearing monads with no causal interaction; mind–body coordination is explained by a divinely pre-established harmony.
records.scope: See cited definition and scope review

records.name: Spinoza’s attribute/mode theory of mind
records.status_note: Often read as dual-aspect monism or neutral monism, but scholarly interpretation is disputed.
records.summary: Mind and body are one individual conceived under the attributes of thought and extension; mental and bodily orders express the same underlying substance without cross-attribute causation.
records.scope: See cited definition and scope review

records.name: Kantian transcendental unity of apperception
records.status_note: Not a neural CT and not equivalent to contemporary higher-order thought theory.
records.summary: Unified experience requires that representations be combinable under a single “I think,” structured by forms of intuition and categories; this is a transcendental account of conditions for experience.
records.scope: See cited definition and scope review

citations.title: SEP: Kant’s View of the Mind and Consciousness of Self

records.name: Jamesian stream of consciousness and radical empiricism
records.status_note: James’s commitments on neutral monism and panpsychism changed; attribute by work/date.
records.summary: Consciousness is a continuous, selective, personal stream; radical empiricism later treats relations as directly experienced and challenges a sharp subject–object split.
records.scope: See cited definition and scope review

records.name: Husserlian transcendental phenomenology
records.status_note: Method, descriptive theory, and transcendental idealism are distinct layers in Husserl’s corpus.
records.summary: Consciousness is intentional and temporally structured; phenomenological reduction investigates how objects, self, and world are constituted in first-person experience.
records.scope: See cited definition and scope review

records.name: Merleau-Ponty’s embodied phenomenology
records.status_note: Influences enactivism but should not be treated as identical with contemporary sensorimotor theory.
records.summary: Perception and subjectivity arise through a pre-reflective lived body embedded in a meaningful world; perceiver and world are relationally intertwined.
records.scope: See cited definition and scope review

records.name: Advaita Vedānta nondual consciousness
records.status: living tradition · philosophical, not empirical CT
records.status_note: Do not collapse all Vedānta into Advaita; Viśiṣṭādvaita and Dvaita reject key Advaita claims.
records.summary: The true self (ātman) is pure, non-intentional consciousness and is numerically identical with brahman; empirical plurality and self-identification are explained through ignorance and appearance.
records.scope: See cited definition and scope review

records.name: Sāṃkhya–Yoga puruṣa/prakṛti dualism
records.status_note: Calling this “mind–body dualism” is only approximate: mind belongs to prakṛti, not to puruṣa.
records.summary: Pure, inactive consciousness (puruṣa) is ontologically distinct from material nature (prakṛti), which includes intellect, ego, mind, cognition, and affect; liberation involves discriminating them.
records.era: Patañjali’s Yoga tradition; first millennium BCE/CE onward
records.scope: See cited definition and scope review

citations.title: SEP: Concept of Emotion in Classical Indian Philosophy

records.name: Nyāya–Vaiśeṣika substantial self theory
records.status_note: Nyāya and Vaiśeṣika merged historically but retain textual and doctrinal differences.
records.summary: An enduring immaterial self is a substance that bears episodic properties such as cognition, desire, effort, pleasure, and pain; consciousness is not the self’s permanent essence in all states.
records.scope: See cited definition and scope review

citations.title: SEP: Personhood in Classical Indian Philosophy
SEP: Concept of Emotion in Classical Indian Philosophy

records.name: Abhidharma no-self and momentary mind analysis
records.status_note: The three main Abhidharma traditions disagree about ontology, time, and cognition; never merge their claims without school-level attribution.
records.summary: Experience is analyzed into causally conditioned momentary dharmas, with no enduring self; detailed taxonomies explain streams of cognition, attention, affect, and awakened consciousness.
records.scope: See cited definition and scope review

citations.title: SEP: Mind in Indian Buddhist Philosophy

records.name: Yogācāra mind-only and eight-consciousness model
records.status_note: Explicitly flag the scholarly idealism debate and differences among Yogācāra texts.
records.summary: Yogācāra develops manifest sensory/mental consciousnesses, afflicted mind, and store consciousness; “mind-only” gives cognition priority, though whether this is ontological idealism is disputed.
records.scope: See cited definition and scope review

records.name: Jaina jīva as unobstructed consciousness
records.status_note: Jaina ontology is pluralist and should not be assimilated to Advaita or generic panpsychism.
records.summary: Each living being embodies an enduring jīva whose intrinsic nature is unobstructed consciousness, cognition, and perception, obscured by karmic matter.
records.era: Umāsvāti and later Jaina thinkers; ancient India–present
records.scope: See cited definition and scope review

records.name: Avicennian immaterial rational soul / Flying Man
records.status_note: Flying Man is an argument about self-awareness and soul, not an empirical deprivation experiment.
records.summary: The rational soul is a self-aware, immaterial, individually enduring substance; the Flying Man thought experiment argues for basic self-awareness independent of sensory body-awareness.
records.scope: See cited definition and scope review

citations.title: SEP: Arabic and Islamic Psychology and Philosophy of Mind

records.name: Theory-Theory of mindreading
records.status: major historical research family · active and contested
records.status_note: Umbrella with modular, “child scientist,” model-based, nativist, and constructivist versions; version separately.
records.summary: People understand and predict action by deploying an implicit folk-psychological theory whose concepts and generalizations relate beliefs, desires, perceptions, emotions, and behavior.
records.era: David Premack and Guy Woodruff; Alison Gopnik, Henry Wellman and others; 1950s–present
records.scope: See cited definition and scope review

records.name: Simulation Theory of mindreading
records.status: major research family · active and contested
records.status_note: High-level, low-level, embodied, and hybrid simulation accounts differ; do not confuse this with the computer-simulation hypothesis.
records.summary: People attribute or predict another’s mental states and decisions by using their own cognitive and affective mechanisms as an offline model of the other, with projection and adjustment.
records.scope: See cited definition and scope review

records.name: Theory-of-Mind Mechanism (ToMM) / modular mindreading
records.status: influential active family · modularity and developmental claims contested
records.status_note: Leslie’s ToMM and Baron-Cohen’s multi-component mindreading system overlap but are not identical architectures.
records.summary: A domain-specific cognitive architecture is proposed to identify agents, represent propositional attitudes, and support early belief–desire reasoning through specialized modular heuristics.
records.era: Simon Baron-Cohen; later Ori Friedman and Tamsin German; 1980s–present
records.scope: See cited definition and scope review

records.name: Intentional Systems Theory / Intentional Stance
records.status: influential framework · realist and instrumentalist readings contested
records.status_note: A predictive/explanatory stance, not a claim that every system so treated is phenomenally conscious.
records.summary: Behavior is predicted by treating a system as a rational agent with beliefs and desires appropriate to its situation, whenever that strategy yields useful patterns.
records.scope: See cited definition and scope review

citations.title: SEP: Folk Psychology as a Theory

records.name: Interaction Theory of social cognition
records.domain: Phenomenology / developmental and embodied social cognition
records.tradition: Phenomenology / developmental and embodied social cognition
records.status_note: Some mental-state reasoning may still use inference or narrative; strong and pluralist interactionist versions differ.
records.summary: Much everyday understanding of others is direct, embodied, and enacted in second-person interaction rather than achieved primarily by detached theorizing or internal simulation.
records.scope: See cited definition and scope review

records.name: Narrative Practice Hypothesis (NPH)
records.status_note: A sociocultural developmental hypothesis about reason explanation, not a general account of all social perception.
records.summary: Children normally acquire mature understanding of reasons for action through supported participation in stories about persons acting for beliefs, desires, and other reasons.
records.scope: See cited definition and scope review

citations.title: The Narrative Practice Hypothesis: Origins and Applications of Folk Psychology

records.name: Extended Mind thesis
records.status: influential active thesis · strongly contested for phenomenal extension
records.status_note: Extended cognition does not by itself establish extended phenomenal consciousness; store that stronger claim separately.
records.summary: Under appropriate coupling and parity conditions, parts of the environment can constitute cognitive processes rather than merely causally support them.
records.scope: See cited definition and scope review

records.name: Phenomenal Intentionality Theory
records.status_note: This is primarily a consciousness-first theory of intentionality, not a standalone production mechanism for consciousness.
records.summary: Some intentional content is constituted or grounded by phenomenal consciousness, giving conscious character an explanatory priority in the theory of mental content.
records.scope: See cited definition and scope review

records.name: Prereflective self-consciousness
records.status: major phenomenological family · interpretation and scope contested
records.status_note: Keep separate from reflective self-knowledge and contemporary higher-order representation theories.
records.summary: Every conscious episode is claimed to involve an implicit first-personal self-givenness prior to introspection, judgment, or explicit higher-order reflection.
records.scope: See cited definition and scope review

records.name: Minimal self and narrative self distinction
records.status_note: Treat minimal self and narrative self as constructs within a framework, not as one neural theory.
records.summary: Distinguishes immediate first-personal ownership and agency from temporally extended, autobiographical, socially mediated selfhood.
records.scope: See cited definition and scope review

records.name: Brentanian intentionality and inner perception
records.status_note: Brentano's secondary-object account should not be merged without qualification into later higher-order theories.
records.summary: Mental acts are object-directed and are conscious through an inseparable secondary awareness of the act itself, intended to avoid an infinite regress of inner observation.
records.scope: See cited definition and scope review

records.name: Locke's consciousness criterion of personal identity
records.status_note: Do not reduce Locke's position to an unqualified memory theory; attribution depends on the relevant passage and interpretation.
records.summary: Personal identity tracks sameness of consciousness extending across actions and thoughts rather than simply sameness of body or immaterial substance.
records.scope: See cited definition and scope review

records.name: Humean bundle and succession account of self
records.status: historically foundational · Hume's own later reservations remain significant
records.status_note: Hume acknowledged unresolved difficulties in his appendix; later bundle theories require separate records.
records.summary: Introspection is said to disclose a changing succession of perceptions rather than an impression of an enduring substantial self.
records.scope: See cited definition and scope review

citations.title: Hume, A Treatise of Human Nature

records.name: Augustinian immediate self-presence
records.status: historical theological psychology · enduring philosophical influence
records.status_note: Separate the immediate self-presence claim from Augustine's Trinitarian analogy and broader theology.
records.summary: The mind is already present to and aware of itself before explicit self-thinking, within an account relating memory, understanding, and love.
records.scope: See cited definition and scope review

records.name: Plotinian Intellect, Soul, and the shifting conscious self
records.status: historical Neoplatonic account · scholarly interpretation active
records.status_note: Distinguish Intellect's self-thinking from the changing center of ordinary human awareness.
records.summary: Intellect is unitary self-intellection identical with its intelligible contents, while embodied human awareness is centered in a representational faculty whose attention can turn toward intelligible or bodily life.
records.scope: See cited definition and scope review

records.name: Hegelian recognition account of self-consciousness
records.status_note: Recognition is a social-developmental condition of self-consciousness, not a neural mechanism of phenomenal awareness.
records.summary: Individual self-consciousness develops through reciprocal recognition by other self-conscious subjects within social and normative structures.
records.scope: See cited definition and scope review

records.name: Bergsonian duration and memory
records.status_note: Keep the phenomenology of duration distinct from Bergson's broader metaphysics and later accounts of memory.
records.summary: Lived consciousness is qualitative, interpenetrating duration rather than a sequence of spatialized instants, with memory carrying the past into present awareness.
records.scope: See cited definition and scope review

records.name: Stein's phenomenology of empathy
records.status_note: More specific than generic interaction theory; do not equate empathy with simulation, emotional contagion, or inference.
records.summary: Empathy is a distinctive, direct but non-original experience through which another embodied subject's experience is given without becoming one's own.
records.scope: See cited definition and scope review

records.name: Cārvāka and Lokāyata embodied materialism
records.status: historical · corpus fragmentary and attribution contested
records.status_note: Surviving views are reconstructed largely from fragments and opponents; do not assign the position confidently to one founder.
records.summary: The person is identified with the living body and consciousness is treated as arising from material organization rather than an independently surviving self.
records.scope: See cited definition and scope review

citations.title: SEP: Personhood in Classical Indian Philosophy

records.name: Madhyamaka emptiness and no-intrinsic-self
records.status: historical and living tradition · internally diverse
records.status_note: This is not a laboratory consciousness theory, and Madhyamaka schools differ over the interpretation of emptiness.
records.summary: Minds, selves, and conscious events lack independent intrinsic nature and exist dependently within a soteriological and dialectical analysis.
records.scope: See cited definition and scope review

records.name: Dignāga–Dharmakīrti reflexive awareness
records.status: historically influential · rejected by major Buddhist interlocutors
records.status_note: Candrakīrti, Śāntideva, and other critics reject intrinsic reflexive awareness; retain opponent-specific claims.
records.summary: Each cognition is held to reveal both its object-appearance and itself nonconceptually through reflexive awareness.
records.scope: See cited definition and scope review

citations.title: SEP archive: Mind in Indian Buddhist Philosophy

records.name: Viśiṣṭādvaita intentional consciousness
records.status_note: This position rejects Advaita's identification of individual consciousness with undifferentiated brahman; do not merge the traditions.
records.summary: Individual selves are real and consciousness is an object-directed property of a knower within a qualified nondual metaphysics.
records.scope: See cited definition and scope review

records.name: Pratyabhijñā recognition philosophy
records.status: historical and living scholarly tradition · non-empirical
records.status_note: Do not collapse Pratyabhijñā into Advaita or generic idealism; its recognition theory and Śaiva commitments are distinct.
records.summary: A single all-encompassing, self-aware consciousness manifests differentiated experience, and liberation is recognition of individual awareness as that universal consciousness.
records.scope: See cited definition and scope review

records.name: Suhrawardī's knowledge by presence
records.status_note: Separate epistemic knowledge-by-presence claims from Suhrawardī's larger ontology of light.
records.summary: Self-awareness and knowledge of certain realities occur through immediate presence rather than an intervening representation, using luminosity as a central metaphysical vocabulary.
records.scope: See cited definition and scope review

citations.title: SEP: Mysticism in Arabic and Islamic Philosophy

records.name: Mullā Ṣadrā's graded consciousness and unity of knower and known
records.status: historical Islamic philosophy · active scholarly tradition
records.status_note: Store separately from Suhrawardī because their ontologies and accounts of substantial change differ substantially.
records.summary: Consciousness is associated with graded existence, and knowing involves a form of identity between knower and known.
records.scope: See cited definition and scope review

citations.title: SEP: Mysticism in Arabic and Islamic Philosophy

records.name: Tathāgatagarbha and luminous-mind family
records.status: historical and living doctrinal family · interpretation disputed
records.status_note: Substantial true-self and dispositional readings must not be blended; text- and school-level claims require separate attribution.
records.summary: Sentient beings possess an ineradicable capacity for awakening, often articulated through mind's luminosity, purity, or Buddha-nature.
records.scope: See cited definition and scope review

records.name: Mahāmudrā empty-luminous mind
records.status_note: Ritual, philosophical, and meditative meanings require separate claims; do not treat Mahāmudrā as one experimentally established state.
records.summary: A family of doctrines and practices in which mind realizes and settles within its empty and luminous nature.
records.scope: See cited definition and scope review

records.name: Dzogchen rigpa and pristine awareness
records.status_note: Do not equate rigpa casually with ordinary attention, generic mindfulness, pure consciousness, or Advaita awareness; Buddhist and Bön systems remain distinguishable.
records.summary: Rigpa denotes a tradition-specific pristine knowing of the ground within Great Perfection systems.
records.scope: See cited definition and scope review

records.name: Zhuangzian heart-mind fasting and responsive awareness
records.status_note: This is not a modern meditation mechanism theory; retain philological and philosophical attribution.
records.summary: Disciplined concepts and heart-mind control can obstruct context-sensitive responsiveness; heart-mind fasting cultivates receptive and embodied responsiveness through qi.
records.scope: See cited definition and scope review

records.name: Wang Yangming's school of heart-mind
records.status_note: The account concerns moral awareness and cultivation, not phenomenal consciousness in the narrow contemporary sense.
records.summary: Pattern is held to be fully present in heart-mind, while innate moral knowing and action form a cultivated unity.
records.scope: See cited definition and scope review

records.name: Akan theories of personhood
records.status: living tradition and active scholarship · major interpretive disagreement
records.status_note: This is not one unified African theory of consciousness; retain interpreter-, language-, and community-specific claims.
records.summary: Accounts relate biological humanity, moral personhood, soul, community, responsibility, and degrees of achieved personhood in different ways.
records.era: modern reconstructions by Kwasi Wiredu, Kwame Gyekye and others
records.scope: See cited definition and scope review

citations.title: SEP: Akan Philosophy of the Person

records.name: Multidimensional global-state framework
records.status: influential active framework · dimensional choices contested
records.status_note: A conceptual state-space framework, not a diagnostic scale or mechanism of consciousness.
records.summary: Global states should be represented through multiple cognitive and behavioral dimensions rather than placed on a single linear level of consciousness.
records.scope: See cited definition and scope review

citations.authors: Tim Bayne, Jakob Hohwy, Adrian M. Owen

records.name: Mesocircuit hypothesis of consciousness recovery
records.status: influential clinical systems hypothesis · actively investigated

records.summary: Recovery after severe brain injury is modeled through changing interactions among central thalamus, striatum, globus pallidus, and frontocortical systems.
records.scope: See cited definition and scope review

citations.title: Recovery of consciousness after brain injury: a mesocircuit hypothesis

records.name: Ipseity-disturbance model of schizophrenia
records.status: influential phenomenological model · contested and non-exhaustive

records.summary: Schizophrenia-spectrum experience is characterized as a disturbance of basic selfhood involving hyperreflexivity and diminished self-affection.
records.scope: See cited definition and scope review

records.name: Fronto-limbic model of depersonalization
records.status: active clinical model · evidence incomplete and heterogeneous
records.status_note: Separate proposed mechanism from the syndrome's diagnostic criteria and from dissociation more broadly.
records.summary: Heightened prefrontal attentional control and reduced limbic and insular affective processing are proposed to contribute to emotional numbing and unreality.

citations.title: Depersonalization: A selective impairment of self-awareness

records.name: REBUS and the Anarchic Brain
records.status_note: REBUS extends predictive-processing ideas to psychedelic action; do not treat all altered-state phenomena as one mechanism.
records.summary: Psychedelics are proposed to relax precision weighting of high-level priors, increasing bottom-up influence and the revisability of entrenched models.

records.name: Cortico-striato-thalamo-cortical altered-state model
records.status_note: Preserve differences between pharmacological psychedelic states and clinical psychosis; similarities do not establish identity.
records.summary: Psychedelic and psychosis-like effects are modeled partly as disrupted thalamocortical gating within cortico-striatal-pallidal-thalamic circuitry.
records.scope: See cited definition and scope review

records.name: AIM model of brain-mind states
records.status: influential state-space model · revised and contested
records.status_note: AIM characterizes state dimensions and is not a complete ontology or mechanism of phenomenal consciousness.
records.summary: Waking, NREM sleep, REM sleep, and related states are located within dimensions of activation, information source, and neuromodulatory mode.
